summary: auth-service token validation began failing with 401 invalid_token at ~14:02 on 2026-04-15, plateauing at ~36% of requests and driving ~21% 5xx at api-gateway; it has not self-recovered. Two auth-service changes landed within one minute: deploy dep-5710 (jjwt 0.11->0.12 breaking parser API, TokenValidator rewritten) at 14:00 and config cfg-2705 (signing-key rotation k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04) at 14:01. Dependencies (user-db, redis-cache), load, CPU/memory and restarts are all flat, ruling out dependency failure and resource/capacity causes. The fault is a partial (not total) failure, which is more consistent with a signing-key mismatch (fraction of tokens) than a uniform code bug in the rewritten validator, and matches historical incident HIST-108. However, because auth-service logs are unavailable (503) and both triggers are within ~1 minute, the two cannot be cleanly separated; the config-change (key rotation) hypothesis is ranked first at moderate confidence with the bad_deployment hypothesis a close second.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Signing-key rotation broke a subset of token validations
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The scheduled auth-service signing-key rotation (cfg-2705, k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01) caused validation to reject tokens still associated with the old key, producing 401 invalid_token for ~1/3 of requests — the same failure mode as HIST-108 (new key id published before all validators/JWKS caches caught up).

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705 rotates signing key k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04
Validators/caches still hold old key, so a fraction of tokens mismatch

assumptions: Some tokens in circulation are still keyed under k-2025-10
JWKS/key propagation lag produces a partial, not total, failure

ranked_hypotheses.title: JWT library upgrade deploy introduced a validation regression
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0, jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 breaking parser API, TokenValidator rewritten at 14:00) introduced a bug that rejects valid tokens, mirroring HIST-109 (library upgrade affecting validation), accepted as 401 invalid_token.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 rewrites TokenValidator with a breaking jjwt API change
New validation logic rejects tokens it previously accepted

assumptions: The rewritten parser fails on a subset of legitimate tokens rather than all of them
No rollback has been attempted yet

ranked_hypotheses.title: Dependency/datastore failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Failure originates in a downstream dependency (user-db, redis-cache) or external provider (kyc-provider).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: user-db connections, redis-cache hit_ratio/connected_clients all flat across onset (F7); no dependency error metrics; failure clearly starts at 14:02 coinciding with auth-service changes (F4).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / capacity saturation on auth-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service ran out of CPU/memory or was saturated by load, causing validation failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: CPU (~38%), memory (~52%), request_rate (~400 req/s) and latency_p99 (~90ms) are flat across onset; restarts=0 (F6); failures are 401s not 5xx from overload.

facts.statement: auth-service error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~36% at 14:02 and plateaued through 15:58.
Deploy dep-5710 rewrote auth-service TokenValidator with a breaking jjwt 0.11->0.12 API change at 14:00.
Config cfg-2705 rotated auth-service signing key k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01.
First 401 invalid_token logged at api-gateway 14:02:22Z on POST /v1/token/validate.
api-gateway 5xx rose to ~21% in the same window (downstream effect).
auth-service CPU, memory, latency, request_rate flat and restarts=0 across onset.
redis-cache and user-db metrics healthy and flat across onset.
HIST-108: prior identical 401/logout incident caused by signing-key rotation vs JWKS propagation.
HIST-109: prior 401 incident after JWT library upgrade, fixed by rollback.
No api-gateway deploy or config change in window.

assumptions: Tokens in circulation are split between the old and new signing keys, enabling a partial failure.
The deploy rollout completed synchronously (restarts=0 means all pods run v7.3.0), so a uniform code bug would fail ~100%.
No rollback of dep-5710 has been attempted; if one had and did not help, H2 would be weakened.

timeline.event: Unrelated deploy dep-5699 (market-data-service v5.0.3) — no correlation to auth symptoms.
auth-service deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0) — jjwt 0.11->0.12 breaking parser API, TokenValidator rewritten.
Config cfg-2705 rotates jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04.
auth-service error_rate jumps to ~37%; first api-gateway 401 invalid_token at 14:02:22Z.
Error rate still ~36%; no recovery, no rollback recorded.

recommended_actions.action: If the signing-key rotation is suspect, revert cfg-2705 to k-2025-10 (or publish the previous key alongside the new one) and observe whether 401s drop.
recommended_actions.rationale: Fastest way to confirm/deny the key-rotation hypothesis; HIST-108 resolution was re-publishing the previous key.

recommended_actions.action: If no improvement after key revert, roll back deploy dep-5710 to v7.2.x and observe recovery.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-109 was resolved by rolling back the JWT library upgrade; separates H2 from H1.

recommended_actions.action: Restore the identity-namespace log pipeline and capture auth-service TokenValidator logs (error type: key-not-found vs signature/clock-skew).
recommended_actions.rationale: The exact rejection reason would cleanly discriminate key-mismatch from parser bug.

recommended_actions.action: Stagger future rotations and deploys of auth-service by a safe interval; add a canary/JWKS-propagation check before full key cutover.
recommended_actions.rationale: Two overlapping changes within 1 minute made root cause ambiguous; HIST-108 recommends staged rotation.

recommended_actions.action: Add an alert on token-validation 401 ratio and a JWKS/key-id match gauge to catch partial validation failures earlier.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 36% partial failure lacked a dedicated signal and went unnoticed for ~10 minutes.

data_gaps: auth-service logs unavailable (backend 503), so the literal validation error (key-not-found vs signature/clock-skew vs parser exception) could not be read — this is the single most discriminating missing datum.
No explicit JWKS/key-propagation telemetry or config subkeys showing which validators loaded which key.
Could not determine the exact traffic split by token key, so the ~36% partial rate is consistent with but not proven to be a token-fraction.
No deployment canary/phased-rollout metadata to confirm whether v7.3.0 was fully or partially rolled out before 14:02.

findings.statement: auth-service error_rate was ~0.2% until 14:00, then jumped to ~36% in the 14:02 bucket and stayed there through 15:58.
auth-service deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0) replaced the JWT library (jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12, breaking parser API) and rewrote TokenValidator, deployed 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z, status live, not rolled back.
A scheduled signing-key rotation cfg-2705 changed auth-service jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z.
api-gateway logs show 401 invalid_token on POST /v1/token/validate starting 2026-04-15T14:02:22Z — first observed error, ~1m22s after the deploy and ~1m22s after the key rotation.
api-gateway 5xx error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~21% in the same 14:00 bucket, consistent with downstream reflection of auth-service validation failures.
auth-service CPU (~38%), memory (~52%), latency_p99 (~90ms) and request_rate (~400 req/s) are all flat across the onset; restarts are 0 throughout.
Dependency datastores are healthy: redis-cache hit_ratio ~96% and connected_clients ~310, user-db connections_active ~25 — all flat across onset.
The failure is partial: ~36% of token validations fail, not 100%, with a steady plateau (no recovery to present).
auth-service logs are unsearchable: query_logs returned backend 503 'unavailable' on all attempts.

Historical incident HIST-108 (2025-10-01) had identical auth-service symptoms (401 invalid_token, users logged out) with root cause a signing-key rotation publishing a new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS.

refs.quote: Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS

findings.statement: Historical incident HIST-109 (2025-07-11) had the same symptom class after a JWT library upgrade (clock-skew default change), resolved by rollback.

refs.quote: JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default

findings.statement: No api-gateway deploy or config change occurred in the window (both lists empty), so the gateway is not itself a change source.

Inference: a uniform code bug in the rewritten TokenValidator would fail essentially all validations on the deployed fleet (restarts=0, so no partial rollout), which is inconsistent with the observed ~36% partial failure; a key-mismatch affecting a subset of tokens better matches a fractional failure.
